about.title: Stanton Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Medical malpractice cases in Stanton, a small city inside Orange County with just under 39,000 residents, often involve local clinics, urgent care centers, and hospitals in the surrounding area. Patients here rely on quick, accurate care, and when a diagnosis is missed, a medication dosage is wrong, or a surgical step is skipped, the consequences can follow someone for years. California's MICRA law shapes how these claims move forward, with strict notice requirements and a discovery-based filing window that make early legal guidance valuable. A bad medical outcome by itself doesn't mean malpractice occurred — proving negligence typically requires a qualified medical expert who can speak to what a reasonably careful provider should have done differently. We can review medical records, evaluate whether your case meets California's standards, and explain the realistic path forward — all without any upfront cost or obligation.

items.title: We Understand the MICRA Clock
items.desc: California generally gives patients one year from discovering the harm, and no more than three years from the injury itself, to act — plus a required 90-day pre-suit notice. Missing these windows can close the door on a claim entirely, so timing matters from day one.

items.title: Expert Review Isn't Optional
items.desc: California law almost always requires a qualified medical expert to establish that a provider's care fell below the accepted standard. Our team works with the kind of medical evaluation these cases demand.

items.title: Damages Rules Are Specific — and Changing
items.desc: Non-economic damage caps under MICRA rise on a statutory schedule each year, which affects how a claim is valued. We can help set realistic expectations from the start with current cap information.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a medical malpractice claim in Stanton?
items.answer: Under California's MICRA rules, you generally have one year from when you discovered — or reasonably should have discovered — the injury, but no more than three years from the date of the injury itself. There's also a 90-day pre-suit notice requirement before a case can be filed. Because these deadlines are strict, it's worth getting a review sooner rather than later.

items.question: Is a poor medical outcome automatically malpractice?
items.answer: No. Medicine involves uncertainty, and not every bad result means a provider was negligent. To have a viable claim, there generally needs to be evidence that a provider deviated from the accepted standard of care, which is why a qualified medical expert almost always has to weigh in.

items.question: My care happened near Beach Boulevard or Katella Avenue in Stanton — does that matter for my claim?
items.answer: The location of the facility itself isn't usually the deciding factor in a malpractice case; what matters more is the medical records, the standard of care, and expert review. That said, we can help you gather the right records quickly if your care took place near these Orange County corridors.

items.question: Do you charge anything upfront?
items.answer: No. We work on a contingency basis, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation. Our initial case review is completely free.
